nodes.title: Scalar maps on locally free arithmetic classes
nodes.statement: For a compatible homomorphism of arithmetic orders Λ→Γ, extension takes locally free rank-n Λ-lattices to locally free rank-n Γ-lattices and induces Cl(Λ)→Cl(Γ), whenever coefficient completions commute with this scalar change. If Γ itself is a locally free Λ-lattice of fixed rank d, restriction induces Cl(Γ)→Cl(Λ). On a rank-n Γ-lattice P its formula is Res(cΓ(P))=cΛ(Res P)−n·cΛ(Res Γ), with Res P of local rank nd. In particular it equals cΛ(Res P) only when the coefficient-order correction class vanishes. Merely being an overorder does not imply the restriction hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the balanced universal property to commute extension with central coefficient completions, then compute on completed free bases. For restriction use Γ_v≅Λ_vᵈ. The defining class [P]−n[Γ] restricts to [Res P]−n[Res Γ]; add and subtract nd[Λ] to obtain cΛ(Res P)−n cΛ(Res Γ). For Z[G]→O_F[G], an integral Z-basis of O_F makes Res Γ globally free of rank [F:Q], so the correction class is zero.

nodes.title: The product identity for invertible ideals
nodes.statement: For a Dedekind domain A with fraction field K and nonzero invertible fractional ideals I,J, I⊕J≅A⊕IJ as A-modules.
proofSteps: I⊕J and A⊕IJ are rank-two lattices in K². GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 classifies such lattices by rank and Steinitz class, and its product and fractional-ideal APIs give st(I⊕J)=[I][J]=[IJ]=st(A⊕IJ); hence the two modules are isomorphic. A direct construction is also available: replace I and J by scaled integral representatives with coprime support, using finite prime avoidance; for coprime representatives the map I⊕J→A, (x,y)↦x+y, is onto with kernel {(z,−z):z∈I∩J=IJ}, and the sequence splits because A is free.
acceptance: For a Dedekind domain A with fraction field K and nonzero invertible fractional ideals I,J, I⊕J≅A⊕IJ as A-modules.

Its inverse sends (n,[I]) to n[A]+([I]−[A]). For a nonfield A this identifies inherited Cl(A) with Additive(ClassGroup A); for a field, ClassGroup A and the rank kernel are both zero, without invoking the vacuous completion definition.
proofSteps: A nonzero finite projective A-module P is an A-lattice in K⊗P, so GN.2's pseudobasis theorem writes it as Aⁿ⁻¹⊕I, and GN.2's Steinitz class is invariant under isomorphism and multiplicative on direct sums; the invariant therefore descends through SplitK0. The product identity proves independence of the ideal representative and additivity of the inverse. The GN.2 decomposition checks the inverse on all finite projective generators; include zero and field branches.

nodes.title: The norm of a projective group-ring module reaches all invariants
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A, finite group G and projective left A[G]-module P, the group norm induces an A-linear isomorphism P_G→P^G from coinvariants to invariants. In particular every invariant m is ∑g∈G gx for some x∈P. Restriction to a subgroup preserves projectivity and the same statement. For a Galois integral lattice the norm is the field trace.
proofSteps: For A[G], coinvariants are A by augmentation, and invariants are A times the group norm; the induced norm sends 1 to that basis element, so it is an isomorphism. Extend to arbitrary free modules and then transport the isomorphism to a projective retract, since norm commutes with the splitting maps. Restriction to H preserves projectivity because A[G] is free over A[H]. Identify the Galois norm with the sum defining the integral trace.
acceptance: For a commutative ring A, finite group G and projective left A[G]-module P, the group norm induces an A-linear isomorphism P_G→P^G from coinvariants to invariants. In particular every invariant m is ∑g∈G gx for some x∈P. Restriction to a subgroup preserves projectivity and the same statement. For a Galois integral lattice the norm is the field trace.

sources.match: For a normal integral basis the trace from the integers onto the fixed integers is surjective, by regrouping the coefficients over cosets; the node extends this norm statement from free modules to all projective group-ring modules.

Tame ambiguous ideals are projective over the group ring by Rim's criterion and hence cohomologically trivial; the node is the degree-zero part of that statement, bijectivity of the norm from coinvariants to invariants for a projective module.

nodes.title: Ideles and lattice gluing for an arithmetic order
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra B over a number field F, an O_F-order Λ and each finite place v, put B_v=F_v⊗B and Λ_v=O_v⊗Λ. J(B) is the restricted product of B_v× with respect to Λ_v×, with full B_v× at infinity; U(Λ) has Λ_v× at finite places and the full B_v× at infinite places. For α∈J(B), I(α)=B∩∏finite-v α_vΛ_v is a full right Λ-lattice with those completions. Left Λ-modules are obtained by applying this construction to Bᵒᵖ,Λᵒᵖ. All ensuing idele formulae use this opposite-algebra convention.
hypotheses: Λ is a full finite torsion-free central O_F-lattice, F a number field.
proofSteps: Only finitely many local lattices differ from Λ_v. Clear denominators and intersect the finitely many modified local conditions; the integral lattice patching in the global-local dictionary proves the completion formula and uniqueness. Changing the reference order changes only finitely many compact open factors.

nodes.title: Reduced norm of a semisimple number-field algebra
nodes.statement: Write B=∏i B_i with centres F_i. Each B_i is central simple, hence Azumaya of rank d_i² over F_i, and Nrd_{B_i}:B_i→F_i is the Azumaya reduced-norm determinant law of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0, the degree-d_i law that becomes the matrix determinant after a splitting. CA.7 assembles these into Nrd=∏Nrd_{B_i}:B→Z(B), restricts to units and extends placewise to completions and ideles. Degree means the square root of dimension over the centre, not dimension over the original base field.
proofSteps: Import the Wedderburn decomposition and, on each simple component, the Azumaya reduced-norm determinant of IHG.0: its uniqueness gives independence of the splitting, and its comparison with the matrix determinant gives multiplicativity and the scalar formula. Take the product over the components. A completion is a scalar extension of each component, so the law base-changes to B_v; reduced norms of order units are units of the centre's integers, which gives the placewise map on ideles.

nodes.title: Local and global reduced-norm images
nodes.statement: For each central simple number-field component C/F, Nrd(C×) consists exactly of a∈F× positive at every real place where C_v is a matrix algebra over Hamilton quaternions. At finite v the image is all F_v×; for a maximal O_v-order its unit image is O_v×. At a ramified real place it is ℝ_{>0}, otherwise the full local centre group. For any finite-place order, its norm-unit image is open. These statements apply componentwise to semisimple B.
proofSteps: Reduce each local simple component to M_r(D). Import the local Brauer invariant and its restriction formula: a degree-d extension kills the invariant of a division algebra D of degree d. The splitting/embedding criterion then embeds both the unramified degree-d extension and a degree-d totally ramified Eisenstein extension as maximal subfields. Their integral rings lie in the unique maximal order of D. Import unramified unit-norm surjectivity from LocalFieldsRamification Layer2 and the norm valuation formula from Layer3: the first supplies every unit and a uniformizer of the second supplies valuation one. Morita invariance and conjugacy of maximal orders give the asserted matrix-order unit image. At infinity compute split-real, complex and quaternionic determinants. For the global step, choose local regular elements with prescribed norm, approximate their separable reduced characteristic polynomials while fixing the constant term, and use prescribed-separable-polynomial to realize that polynomial globally. Split places supply companion matrices. This is Kneser’s §5.4 proof using the global Brauer splitting criterion. Openness follows from the reduced trace on sufficiently deep principal units.

nodes.title: The reduced-norm-one group scheme
nodes.statement: For a central simple F-algebra C, SL₁(C) is the affine F-group whose points over every commutative F-algebra T are ker((C⊗F T)×→T×) under the reduced norm polynomial. nodes.title: Eichler’s condition for semisimple algebras
nodes.statement: A semisimple number-field algebra B satisfies Eichler’s condition iff none of its simple components is itself a quaternion division algebra over a totally real centre ramified at every real place. proofSteps: Use the Wedderburn components, their centres and real completions. Make the excluded matrix size r=1 explicit. The predicate is invariant under algebra isomorphism and opposite algebra.

nodes.title: Inner forms meet the strong-approximation hypotheses
nodes.statement: For a central simple C/F of degree d>1, SL₁(C) is connected semisimple and simply connected. Its archimedean product is noncompact unless C is itself a totally definite quaternion division algebra. Consequently, if semisimple B satisfies Eichler’s condition, J(B)′=B×′·(J(B)′∩U(Γ)) for every arithmetic order Γ, including every idele-conjugate order. Trivial field factors are omitted.
proofSteps: After a splitting field this is SL_d; descend the connected, semisimple and simply connected properties through the inner form. Inspect C⊗ℝ: SL_d(ℝ), SL_d(ℂ), or quaternionic SL_r; the sole compact nontrivial case is r=1 over ℍ. Apply AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 with S the archimedean places and the compact open intersection with Γ-units. The inner-form identification is PRR Proposition2.37: a splitting trivialization gives an inner cocycle in PGL_d and descent of the determinant-one equations. Geometric connectedness and simple connectedness are preserved by this form. Explicit diagonal one-parameter subgroups prove noncompactness in all allowed real or complex matrix cases.

nodes.title: Stable idele classification in every semisimple case
nodes.statement: For an arithmetic order Λ in semisimple B, its locally free stable class group is J(B)/(J(B)′ B× U(Λ)). For each m≥2, locally free rank-m lattices are classified by this quotient via their GL_m(B) adelic basis matrices and reduced norms. No decomposition into rank-one ideals is assumed in constructing this classification. No Eichler hypothesis on B is needed. The quotient is abelian and identifies with inherited Cl(Λ) inside projective K₀.
proofSteps: First classify rank m by GL_m(B)\J(M_m(B))/GL_m(Λ). Semilocal elimination gives the same reduced-norm image for Λ_v× and GL_m(Λ_v). Since M_m(B) satisfies Eichler for m≥2, strong approximation removes its norm-one fibre. The stable equality theorem identifies equal stable classes in SplitK0 with these stabilized isomorphisms. To ensure no loss from the ambient projective K₀ use a finite free complement of every projective stabilization witness.

nodes.title: Positive-rank locally free lattices split off free summands
nodes.statement: Every locally free rank-m lattice M over an arithmetic order Λ in a semisimple number-field algebra, with m≥1, is isomorphic to Λᵐ⁻¹⊕I for a locally free rank-one integral one-sided ideal I. For left modules I is a left ideal. The condition m≥1 is essential. This statement does not assume Eichler’s condition.
proofSteps: For m≥2 use local free bases and a generic B-basis of M to obtain an idele of M_m(B). Choose an idele α of B with the same reduced norm, using the local norm-image theorem componentwise. Glue I(α). The lattices M and Λᵐ⁻¹⊕I(α) have the same norm class in the rank-m classification and are therefore isomorphic. For m=1 glue M directly by its local bases. Clear central denominators to make I integral. This proof uses matrix strong approximation and never invokes a hereditary maximal-order splitting theorem.

nodes.title: Jacobinski cancellation under Eichler’s condition
nodes.statement: Let Λ be an arithmetic order in a semisimple number-field algebra satisfying Eichler’s condition. Locally free left Λ-lattices P,Q of the same rank with [P]=[Q] in projective K₀ are isomorphic. Equivalently, P⊕Λᵏ≅Q⊕Λᵏ implies P≅Q. The rank-zero case is zero. nodes.title: Local–global realization of separable reduced characteristic polynomials
nodes.statement: Let C/F be central simple of degree d and f∈F[X] monic separable of degree d. There is c∈C with reduced characteristic polynomial f iff every local C_v has such an element; equivalently C splits over F[X]/g for every irreducible factor g of f. For a prescribed nonzero norm a, local witnesses can be chosen regular and their polynomials approximated with the constant coefficient (−1)ᵈa fixed.
proofSteps: For a separable algebra E=F[X]/f, its embedding in C with total degree d is equivalent to splitting each simple field factor; use simple-module dimension to prove both directions. Apply the global Brauer injectivity theorem over each field factor to convert local splitting into global splitting. Regularize a local norm witness by multiplying generic commutators; nonvanishing of the discriminant is a nonempty open condition over an infinite field. Weak approximation of the remaining polynomial coefficients preserves local finite étale algebra types at the finite set of nonsplit places, by Newton/Krasner stability; at split places use a companion matrix.

nodes.title: Semilocal elimination preserves the determinant image
nodes.statement: For a semilocal ring R and n≥1, GL_n(R) is generated by elementary matrices and diagonal matrices with entries in R×. Consequently for a finite-place arithmetic order Λ_v, Nrd(GL_n(Λ_v))=Nrd(Λ_v×). For a semilocal group ring, matrix character-determinant images likewise equal unit character-determinant images.
proofSteps: Reduce a unimodular row modulo the Jacobson radical to the product of matrix rings over division rings. Elementary column operations make the first entry a unit in every simple quotient; lift them and use the unit criterion modulo the radical. Clear the first column and row and induct on n. Elementary matrices have determinant one in every splitting representation; multiply the diagonal unit determinants.

nodes.title: Determinants indexed by virtual characters
nodes.statement: For a finite group G and a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra admitting a splitting field E, Det(u)(χ)=det(ρ_χ(u)) for u a group-algebra unit and χ an actual E-character. Extend multiplicatively to the virtual character group R_G, using inverses for negative coefficients. With the valuewise absolute Galois action this is an equivariant homomorphism whenever u is defined over the base field; do not confuse Det(u) with the one-dimensional character detχ of G.
proofSteps: Independence of a representation follows from isomorphism invariance and semisimple character classification. Direct sums multiply determinants, giving descent to virtual characters. Galois conjugation acts on the coefficients of the representation, and the reduced-norm splitting identity gives the centre-coordinate interpretation.

nodes.title: Absolute and relative norm resolvents
nodes.statement: For a G-Galois number-field extension L/F and normal generator a, form r_G(a)=∑g∈G g(a)g⁻¹∈L[G]× and (a|χ)=Det(r_G(a))(χ). For absolute ℤ[G] classes apply the character-hom norm N_F/ℚ: (N f)(χ)=∏ω f(χ^{ω⁻¹})^ω, over a right transversal of Ω_F in Ω_ℚ. Use the same construction on semilocal integral generators a_v and take their ratio against a rational normal generator. The absolute integer-ring rank is [F:ℚ], not one unless F=ℚ.
proofSteps: Normal-basis invertibility supplies the resolvent unit. Representation determinants supply character additivity and the twisted Galois rule. Norming the homomorphism over embeddings makes the absolute representative; a transversal change differs by a group determinant, so only its quotient class is canonical. The ratio of local and rational norm resolvents is the adelic basis matrix determinant.

nodes.title: Normal bases and invertible resolvents
nodes.statement: For a finite G-Galois algebra E/F and a∈E, the F[G]-map sending g to g(a) is bijective iff r_G(a)=Σg g(a)g⁻¹ is a unit in E[G]. Over a DVR, an integral resolvent is a unit in O_E[G] iff the integral algebra is étale and a is an integral normal-basis generator; this integral-unit criterion is not asserted for ramified tame extensions.
proofSteps: After scalar extension to a splitting field the regular multiplication matrix of the resolvent is the normal-basis conjugate matrix up to row and column permutations. A nonzero determinant is exactly bijectivity over the field. Over the integral ring invertibility is equivalent to a unit determinant, which is the discriminant criterion for the basis and étaleness.

nodes.title: Stickelberger’s finite Gauss-sum valuation
nodes.statement: Let q=pᶠ, P be a prime above p in Q(ζ_p,ζ_(q−1)), ω the Teichmüller character for its residue F_q, and ψ(x)=ζ_p^Tr(x). If 0≤a<q−1 has digits a_i, put s=Σa_i and h=∏a_i!. Then h·(−gaussSum(ω⁻ᵃ,ψ))≡(ζ_p−1)ˢ mod Pˢ⁺¹. Thus v_P(gaussSum)=s when v_P(ζ_p−1)=1, and the valuation with v_p(p)=1 is s/(p−1). The trivial-character case a=0 has valuation zero.
proofSteps: Expand normalized Jacobi sums modulo P using finite-field power sums; only the congruent exponents survive. Comparing coefficients in (1+ΣX_i)^m in characteristic p gives the digitwise multinomial congruence. Prove the a=1 base case directly: expand ζ_p^Tr(x) modulo (ζ_p−1)² and use Σx≠0 x⁻¹Tr(x)=−1 in F_q; this replaces Conrad’s unread Washington reference. Apply the two-Gauss double-sum identity to Jacobi sums, induct through the one-digit exponents, and use invariance under Frobenius to assemble the digits. The leading factorial is a unit, so the congruence gives the exact valuation.
acceptance: Let q=pᶠ, P be a prime above p in Q(ζ_p,ζ_(q−1)), ω the Teichmüller character for its residue F_q, and ψ(x)=ζ_p^Tr(x). If 0≤a<q−1 has digits a_i, put s=Σa_i and h=∏a_i!. Then h·(−gaussSum(ω⁻ᵃ,ψ))≡(ζ_p−1)ˢ mod Pˢ⁺¹. Thus v_P(gaussSum)=s when v_P(ζ_p−1)=1, and the valuation with v_p(p)=1 is s/(p−1). The trivial-character case a=0 has valuation zero.

nodes.title: The Hasse–Davenport product relation
nodes.statement: For F_q, a nontrivial additive character ψ, n≥1 dividing q−1, a multiplicative character λ of exact order n and any multiplicative χ (all extended by zero at zero), write g(θ)=gaussSum(θ,ψ). Then g(χⁿ)·∏_(j=1)^(n−1)g(λʲ)=χ(n)ⁿ·∏_(j=0)^(n−1)g(χλʲ). The trivial multiplicative character has g(1)=−1, so including j=0 in the left product changes the sign. The weak form, equality up to a root of unity, is the form Taylor’s logarithmic computation uses.
proofSteps: Reduce ψ to the trace-normalized additive character by the pinned scaling formula; both sides change by the same character value. The ratio R of the two sides has absolute value one at every complex embedding: nontrivial Gauss sums have absolute value √q, the trivial one is −1, and the two sides contain the same number of trivial factors. It is a unit at every prime above p by finite-gauss-valuation, because the digit-sum valuations agree by the fractional-part identity Σ_j{x+j/n}={nx}+(n−1)/2. Gauss sums are divisible only by primes above p, so R is an algebraic unit all of whose conjugates have absolute value one, hence a root of unity by Kronecker’s theorem. This weak form needs no further input.

For the exact form, gaussSum_mulShift_eq shows that ζ_p↦ζ_p^b, for b∈F_p×, multiplies both sides by the same character value, so R lies in ℚ(ζ_(q−1)). Comparing the leading Stickelberger residues with the digit-factorial multiplication gives R≡1 modulo a prime above p. For p odd every root of unity in ℚ(ζ_(q−1)) has order prime to p and is determined by its residue, so R=1. For p=2 the field contains −1, which is ≡1 modulo 2, so the residue does not fix the sign: this residual sign is the boundary G-DH.
acceptance: For F_q, a nontrivial additive character ψ, n≥1 dividing q−1, a multiplicative character λ of exact order n and any multiplicative χ (all extended by zero at zero), write g(θ)=gaussSum(θ,ψ). Then g(χⁿ)·∏_(j=1)^(n−1)g(λʲ)=χ(n)ⁿ·∏_(j=0)^(n−1)g(χλʲ). The trivial multiplicative character has g(1)=−1, so including j=0 in the left product changes the sign. The weak form, equality up to a root of unity, is the form Taylor’s logarithmic computation uses.

nodes.title: Tame local Galois Gauss sums
nodes.statement: Fix a finite extension F/Q_p, ψ_F=exp(2πi·Tr_F/Q_p(−)) with the usual rational p-adic additive character, and the local Artin convention of ClassFieldTheory. For a ramified one-dimensional finite-order character χ of conductor ideal fχ choose c generating D_F/Q_p·fχ and set τ_F(χ)=Σ_(u∈(O_F/fχ)×) χ(Art_F(u/c))ψ_F(u/c). For unramified χ set τ_F(χ)=χ(D_F/Q_p)⁻¹. Extend multiplicatively to virtual characters using the local-constant induction rule with its degree correction, and form the global finite product τ(χ). Independence and existence of this extension require G-LOCALCONSTANTS.
proofSteps: For degree one the conductor determines a finite sum independent of lifts; a change of generator is cancelled by character and additive-character reindexing. Import local Artin and conductor carriers. To extend beyond degree one use Brauer induction and the local-constant induction factor, checking all relations rather than choosing a Brauer expression arbitrarily. The unread relation/induction proof is explicitly G-LOCALCONSTANTS.

Apply the same character transport to the resolvent, where the group element changes its determinant by the inverse factor.

The assertion includes virtual characters and the coefficient-field embedding norm; valuations may be nonzero.

For a cyclic Kummer extension of inertia degree e, the eigenresolvent valuation is the least nonnegative residue t/e. Unramified characters have zero valuation; multiplying a normal generator by a group-ring unit leaves these valuations unchanged.

nodes.title: Symplectic Artin root signs
nodes.statement: For a global actual character χ set W∞(χ)=∏_(v infinite)i^(−n₋(χ,v)), with n₋ the multiplicity of the negative conjugation eigenspace, and define the algebraic root factor W(χ)=(Nfχ)¹ᐟ²/(τ(χ)W∞(χ)), using the positive real square root. This equals the Artin functional-equation root factor by F76 (2.4)–(2.5). Define W_G on irreducibles to be this value on symplectic irreducibles and 1 on all others, and extend multiplicatively to R_G.
proofSteps: Import the Frobenius–Schur classification, local conductors and conjugation eigenspaces. The inverse Gauss formula fixes the convention without a complex-conjugation guess. The local/global symplectic duality identities give signs and tame Galois invariance via symplectic-root-sign-law. Comparison with analytic Artin functional equations is the explicit G-ARTIN boundary; the algebraic definition does not depend on having formalized Artin L-functions.

nodes.title: The integral group logarithm
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, R a characteristic-zero integral domain, p-torsion-free and p-adically complete, with an endomorphism F satisfying F(r)≡rᵖ mod pR. Let G be a finite p-group, I the augmentation ideal of R[G], C_G its conjugacy classes and φ:R[G]→R[C_G] the additive class projection. Set Ψ(r[g])=F(r)[gᵖ] on the class module and L(1+x)=(p−Ψ)φ(log(1+x)), x∈I. The logarithm converges in Frac(R)[G] because I mod p is nilpotent. Ψ is semilinear on the class module; it is not a ring homomorphism on a nonabelian group ring. Use ν=p⁻¹L on determinant classes where integrality permits.
proofSteps: Augmentation nilpotence modulo p gives I^N⊆pR[G], hence logarithmic convergence in R[1/p][G]. Project to conjugacy classes so logarithms are additive on products. Frobenius cancels denominators by group-log-integrality. For coefficientwise F_R on R[G], the exact character formula is χ(L(u))=p·log Det(u)(χ)−log Det(F_R(u))(ψᵖχ). F_R acts on coefficients before character evaluation; no extension of F_R fixing character roots is assumed. CPT denotes the map induced by L itself by ν; our normalized ν=L/p has image φ(A), while CPT’s ν has image pφ(A).

nodes.title: Local rational Brauer reduction for determinant quotients
nodes.statement: Let R be a normal noetherian characteristic-zero integral domain, p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with a Frobenius lift. For a finite G, the determinant-quotient test reduces to Q_p-p-elementary subgroups C⋊P, with P a p-group and C cyclic of order prime to p, whose conjugation action is the Q_p cyclotomic Galois action. Restriction and integral-character twisting are initially operations on matrix determinant images. The local rational induction identity has multiplier prime to p, invertible on the pro-p quotient after radical reduction. For semilocal group rings matrix and unit conditions agree. The field-of-definition refinements of generic Brauer induction — the prime-to-p multiplier identity over Q_p-p-elementary subgroups, the integral identity over Q_p-ℓ-elementary subgroups for all primes ℓ, and their ℚ-rational analogues used by Taylor — are G-LOCALBRAUER.

A quotient detected modulo the radical is pro-ℓ, hence multiplication by the prime-to-ℓ integer is invertible. For Taylor’s off-diagonal proof, the Q-elementary reduction and twists are applied before the same ℓ-adic quotient argument.

nodes.title: Fixed-point descent for integral determinant units
nodes.statement: Let R⊆S be normal noetherian characteristic-zero integral domains, p-torsion-free and p-adically complete, each with its own lift of Frobenius. Suppose S is finite free over R, Frac(S)/Frac(R) is Galois with finite group Δ, S^Δ=R and Tr_S/R is onto R. For any finite G, Det(S[G]×)^Δ=Det(R[G]×). For a p-group G the fixed-point theorem holds under the domain, completeness, Frobenius, finite-free Galois and invariant hypotheses without the extra normal/noetherian/trace assumptions. The two Frobenius lifts need not commute with the inclusion.
proofSteps: For p-groups use the logarithm on the commutator determinant subgroup and its exact integral image; handle group-element torsion separately. Descend abelian units by taking invariants in the augmentation sequence (p-group-determinant-fixed-point).

For Q_p-p-elementary groups use crossed-product descent (CPT Theorem6.4). For an arbitrary G, the prime-to-p multiplier induction over Q_p-p-elementary subgroups shows that every element of Det(GL(S[G]))^Δ/Det(GL(R[G])) has finite order prime to p (CPT Theorem6.5); ell-elementary-determinant-descent shows that its order is prime to every ℓ≠p (CPT Theorems6.6–6.7). Hence the quotient is trivial, and matrix and unit determinant images agree by general-group-determinant-stability. Trace surjectivity is retained for the general coefficient statement; do not extrapolate the abbreviated survey hypothesis list.

nodes.title: Taylor’s congruences detect the residual determinant torsion
nodes.statement: For the crossed-product Gauss factor f in gauss-log-image, let z and T′ be its commutator and abelian lifts. The quotient f/Det(zT′) lies in Det(G). Taylor’s four integral congruence families force this quotient to be trivial: induced characters of degree greater than two; degree-two characters with semiabelian action; degree-two inversion action; and degree-two semidihedral action. Hence f is an integral-unit determinant, rather than merely having the logarithm of one.
proofSteps: For induced characters compare Gauss factors and determinants against the transfer/cotransfer character at the next index-ℓ subgroup. For degree two the semiabelian branch compares modulo 2 times the radical; the inversion branch compares Gauss factors modulo 4 and determinants modulo 2 times the radical; the semidihedral branch uses the corresponding trace relation modulo 4. Group-element torsion is evaluated on these detecting characters, and the congruences eliminate it by induction on the group. Taylor §§9–10 prove these families, but the crucial degree>2 Gauss congruence invokes Fröhlich–Taylor 1980 §5.1: G-FTCONGRUENCE records that unread supplier. No injectivity of the unrestricted logarithm is used.

nodes.statement: For a tame local G-Galois extension at a rational prime p and ℓ≠p, put K=Q(ζ_p). nodes.title: Trace through the prime-power filtration
nodes.statement: Let A⊆B be finite Dedekind domains and p a nonzero prime of A. nodes.title: Normal integral bases descend by trace to fixed fields
nodes.statement: Let A be integrally closed with fraction field F, L/F finite G-Galois, and B its finite integral closure. nodes.title: Central flat scalar change for finite-order Hom modules
nodes.statement: Let A be commutative noetherian, Λ a finite central A-algebra, M a finitely presented left Λ-module, N any left Λ-module and S a flat commutative A-algebra. The canonical map S⊗ₐHom_Λ(M,N)→Hom_(S⊗ₐΛ)(S⊗ₐM,S⊗ₐN) is an isomorphism, compatible with composition and pure tensors. If S is faithfully flat, projectivity of S⊗M descends to M. nodes.title: Dedekind completions jointly detect finite-module equality
nodes.statement: For a nonfield Dedekind domain A with fraction field F and a nonzero prime v, let Â_v be the valuation ring v.adicCompletionIntegers F. The canonical map A_v→Â_v is a flat local homomorphism and hence faithfully flat. The family A→Â_v therefore detects exactness of finitely generated A-modules and of maps between them; finite sublattice equality and finite-order projectivity descent are applications. For number fields it agrees with the arithmetic completion dictionary of NumberFieldArithmetic Layer5.
proofSteps: The pinned A-algebra structure on Â_v sends a∈A to its image in the completion. Elements outside v have valuation one, so they are units of Â_v and the map factors through A_v. The maximal ideal of A_v maps into the maximal ideal of the valuation subring Â_v, a local ring, so A_v→Â_v is local. Â_v is torsion-free over A by a pinned instance, hence flat over the Dedekind domain A by IsDedekindDomain.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot, hence flat over A_v. Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom makes A_v→Â_v faithfully flat. Localizations at all maximal ideals detect exactness, and every maximal ideal of the nonfield Dedekind domain A is nonzero, so the completions do too. nodes.title: Balanced induction and the finite coset model
nodes.statement: Let S be a commutative ring, G a finite group, H≤G and M a left S[H]-module. There is a canonical S[G]-linear isomorphism S[G]⊗_(S[H])M with functions f:G→M satisfying f(gh)=h⁻¹f(g), on which G acts by left translation. nodes.title: One trace-dual lattice bounds every overorder
nodes.statement: Let A be integrally closed noetherian with fraction field F, B finite-dimensional with nondegenerate regular trace pairing, and Λ an A-order. Choose an F-basis e_i inside Λ and r=det(Tr_reg(e_ie_j))≠0. Every overorder Γ⊇Λ is contained in r⁻¹Σ_i A e_i. nodes.title: Integral composita under arithmetic disjointness
nodes.statement: For finite extensions L/F and K/F of number fields or p-adic fields that are linearly disjoint and have coprime relative discriminant ideals, multiplication induces O_L⊗_(O_F)O_K≅O_(LK). If both are Galois, restriction gives Gal(LK/F)≅Gal(L/F)×Gal(K/F), and tensoring their normal integral bases gives the product normal integral basis. Trivial field intersection alone is not used as linear disjointness unless a Galois hypothesis justifies it.

nodes.title: A single tame cyclotomic conductor cut

nodes.title: The norm-two ideal in Z[√−5] is nonprincipal
nodes.statement: For A=Z[√−5], I=(2,1+√−5) has quotient A/I≅F₂ and norm 2. It is nonprincipal: a principal generator a+b√−5 would have norm a²+5b²=2, which has no integer solution. Consequently I is locally free of rank one but not free, and [I]−[A] is a nonzero class in K₀(A).
